explanation: Simple fluid is T1 dark and T2 bright; fat is bright on both T1 and T2 and suppresses on STIR. Blood changes signal predictably with age, which allows dating of a haemorrhage.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (white matter lesions of brain visualised by CT and MRI), 2020 INI-CET (SWI for microhaemorrhage)

subject: Radiology
stem: Diffusion-weighted imaging shows restricted diffusion in all EXCEPT
explanation: Arachnoid cysts follow CSF signal and do not restrict, which distinguishes them from **epidermoid** cysts, which do. Restriction in acute infarct appears within minutes, long before CT change.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG (ring enhancing lesion with restriction on DWI — abscess), 2021 NEET-PG (lacunar infarct on CT)

subject: Radiology
stem: The imaging modality of choice for acute cholecystitis is
options: Ultrasound, showing wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid and a sonographic Murphy sign
explanation: A wall above 3 mm with stones and a positive sonographic Murphy sign has high accuracy. **HIDA scintigraphy** is the next step when ultrasound is equivocal.
exam: 2015 AIIMS (non-visualisation of gall bladder in scintigraphy — acute cholecystitis), 2023 INI-CET (Phrygian cap, 2X)

subject: Radiology
stem: Liver calcification can be caused by
options: Old granulomatous infection, healed hydatid disease and haemangioma
explanation: Healed tuberculosis and histoplasmosis, calcified hydatid, haemangioma with phleboliths, and treated metastases — particularly mucinous colorectal and ovarian — are the recognised causes.
exam: 2015 AIIMS (calcifications in liver — hepatic adenoma, haemangioma), 2020 INI-CET (crumpled membrane in hydatid, 2X)

subject: Radiology
stem: Target sign and pseudokidney sign on abdominal ultrasound in a toddler indicate
explanation: Concentric rings in transverse section give the target or doughnut sign, and the longitudinal view gives the pseudokidney. Pneumatic or hydrostatic reduction is the treatment in a stable child.
exam: 2019 NEET-PG (claw sign is useful in intussusception, 2X), 2023 NEET-PG (hypertrophic pyloric stenosis on USG)

subject: Radiology
stem: The coffee-bean sign on abdominal radiography indicates
explanation: A massively distended loop with an inner cleft resembles a coffee bean, arising from the pelvis towards the right upper quadrant. A **bird-beak** taper appears on contrast enema, and flexible sigmoidoscopic decompression is the first treatment.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (large bowel obstruction with haustrations), 2020 INI-CET (gastric volvulus, 2X)

subject: Radiology
stem: The investigation of choice for suspected acute appendicitis in an adult is
options: Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen, with ultrasound preferred in children and pregnancy
explanation: CT shows a dilated appendix above 6 mm with wall thickening, periappendiceal fat stranding and an appendicolith. Ultrasound avoids radiation but is operator-dependent and limited by body habitus.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (FAST and abdominal imaging in trauma), 2024 INI-CET (ulcerative colitis on CT)

subject: Radiology
stem: Pneumatosis intestinalis with portal venous gas in a preterm neonate indicates
explanation: Intramural gas is diagnostic, and **portal venous gas** or pneumoperitoneum indicates advanced disease needing surgery. Bell staging guides management, and breast milk with cautious feeding is protective.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (Rigler sign in pneumoperitoneum, 3X), 2023 NEET-PG (congenital hypertrophic pyloric stenosis)

subject: Radiology
stem: The bone most commonly affected by Paget disease, and its characteristic early radiographic sign, are
options: The pelvis; osteoporosis circumscripta in the skull and a flame-shaped lytic front in long bones
explanation: The lytic phase is followed by mixed and sclerotic phases with cotton-wool skull, picture-frame vertebra and cortical thickening. Alkaline phosphatase is markedly raised, and sarcomatous change is the feared complication.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (ivory vertebra in Paget's), 2017 AIIMS (sunburst appearance not seen in Paget)

subject: Radiology
stem: The Looser zone on radiography indicates
options: Osteomalacia, as an incomplete lucent pseudofracture perpendicular to the cortex
explanation: It occurs in the medial femoral neck, pubic rami, ribs and scapula. Osteomalacia also gives coarse trabeculae and a generalised loss of definition, with low calcium and phosphate and raised alkaline phosphatase.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (investigations in osteoporosis), 2018 AIIMS (radiological features of rickets, 2X)

subject: Radiology
stem: NEXUS criteria are used to decide
options: Whether cervical spine imaging can be omitted after trauma
The grade of a cerebral arteriovenous malformation
The need for CT in head injury only
explanation: Imaging can be omitted when there is no midline tenderness, no focal deficit, normal alertness, no intoxication and no distracting injury. The Canadian C-spine rule is the alternative decision tool.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (NEXUS criteria is used for cervical spine injury)

subject: Radiology
stem: Whole-body CT in a major trauma patient includes
options: CT of the brain, cervical spine, thorax, abdomen and pelvis
explanation: Pan-scanning shortens time to diagnosis in polytrauma, at the cost of radiation. It is performed only in a **haemodynamically stable** patient; instability mandates immediate intervention instead.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (whole body CT in RTA will include CT brain, cervical spine, thorax, abdomen)

subject: Radiology
stem: Radiological features of skeletal involvement in neurofibromatosis type 1 include
options: Posterior vertebral scalloping, sphenoid wing dysplasia and ribbon ribs
explanation: Dural ectasia causes the scalloping, and tibial pseudoarthrosis with anterolateral bowing is the other classic skeletal feature. Kyphoscoliosis is common.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (radiological feature of skeletal involvement in NF-1 — posterior scalloping of vertebra, sphenoid dysplasia)

subject: Radiology
stem: One vertebra slipping forwards over the one below on a lateral radiograph is
explanation: Meyerding grades it by the percentage of slip, commonly at L5 over S1. A lucency in the pars interarticularis on oblique views gives spondylolysis, which may precede the slip.
exam: 2019 NEET-PG (X-ray shows one vertebra slipping over the other — spondylolisthesis), 2014 AIIMS (slippage of L4 forwards — spondylolisthesis)

subject: Radiology
stem: White matter lesions of the brain are best visualised by
options: MRI, particularly FLAIR sequences, with CT far less sensitive
explanation: FLAIR suppresses CSF signal so periventricular lesions stand out, which is why MRI is the modality for multiple sclerosis, small vessel disease and leukodystrophy.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (white matter lesions of brain can be visualised by CT and MRI)

subject: Radiology
stem: A neonate with heart failure, an enlarging fontanelle and a cranial bruit has
explanation: A high-flow arteriovenous shunt into the deep venous system causes high-output cardiac failure and hydrocephalus. **Endovascular embolisation** is the treatment, and it is the commonest cause of neonatal heart failure from a cerebral cause.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (neonate with CHF, enlarging fontanelle, bruit — vein of Galen malformation, 2X)

subject: Radiology
stem: A preterm baby with jaundice, hepatosplenomegaly and periventricular calcification has
explanation: **Periventricular** calcification with microcephaly indicates CMV, whereas toxoplasmosis gives **scattered** parenchymal calcification with hydrocephalus. CMV is the commonest congenital infection and cause of non-syndromic deafness.
exam: 2022 NEET-PG (preterm baby with jaundice, hepatosplenomegaly, periventricular calcification — CMV infection)

subject: Radiology
stem: The investigation showing contrast outlining the spinal cord on a lateral neck radiograph is
explanation: Intrathecal contrast outlines the cord and roots. It has largely been replaced by MRI, and survives as CT myelography where MRI is contraindicated or a CSF leak must be localised.
exam: 2022 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (lateral view X-ray neck shows contrast outlining spinal cord — myelography, 2X)

subject: Radiology
stem: The investigation in which contrast is injected through a cannula into the biliary tree percutaneously is
explanation: It is used for proximal or hilar obstruction and when ERCP fails or the anatomy is altered after surgery. It permits drainage and stenting, with bleeding and sepsis as the main complications.
exam: 2019 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (investigation in which contrast is injected via cannula — percutaneous biliary drainage, 2X)

subject: Radiology
stem: An angiogram showing an artery giving multiple branches from its left side supplying the small bowel is the
explanation: Jejunal and ileal branches arise from its left and the colic branches from its right. Its origin at about L1 and the aortomesenteric angle are relevant to Wilkie syndrome and to mesenteric ischaemia.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (angiography of abdomen shows artery giving branches — superior mesenteric artery, 2X)

subject: Radiology
stem: A bedridden patient with sudden breathlessness has CT showing a filling defect in a pulmonary artery. The diagnosis is
explanation: CT pulmonary angiography is the investigation of choice. A Westermark sign, Hampton hump and Fleischner sign are the insensitive plain-film findings, and a ventilation–perfusion scan is used in pregnancy and renal failure.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (bedridden patient with sudden SOB, CT shows filling defect — pulmonary embolism, 2X)

subject: Radiology
stem: A high-grade fever with foul-smelling sputum and a thick-walled lung cavity containing an air-fluid level indicates
explanation: Foul-smelling sputum indicates anaerobic infection, usually from aspiration, so the dependent segments are affected — the posterior upper and superior lower lobe segments in a supine patient.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG (high grade fever, foul smelling sputum, lung cavity with air fluid level — lung abscess)

subject: Radiology
stem: Ptosis, muscle weakness, dysphagia and engorged chest wall veins with an anterior mediastinal mass indicate
options: Thymoma with myasthenia gravis and superior vena cava obstruction
explanation: About 10 to 15% of myasthenia patients have a thymoma, and all need CT of the chest. The four Ts of an anterior mediastinal mass are thymoma, teratoma, thyroid and terrible lymphoma.
exam: 2022 NEET-PG (ptosis, muscle weakness, dysphagia, engorged veins — thymoma with myasthenia gravis)

subject: Radiology
stem: A 65-year-old smoker with a lung mass should have which investigation to assess **distant** staging?
explanation: It detects nodal and distant disease that CT misses and prevents futile thoracotomy. Brain imaging is added separately, since physiological cortical uptake limits PET sensitivity for cerebral metastases.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (CECT for lung carcinoma, MRI for Pancoast tumour), 2014 AIIMS (prophylactic craniospinal radiation in small cell lung cancer)

subject: Radiology
stem: The Hounsfield value distinguishing a benign from an indeterminate adrenal adenoma on non-contrast CT is
options: Below 10 HU, indicating a lipid-rich adenoma
explanation: Intracytoplasmic lipid lowers attenuation. Lesions above 10 HU need washout studies on delayed contrast imaging, and **biopsy is avoided until phaeochromocytoma is excluded biochemically**.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (water has zero Hounsfield number), 2023 NEET-PG (mediastinal mass with −62 HU)

subject: Radiology
stem: The ultrasound finding that best predicts malignancy in a complex ovarian cyst is
options: Solid components with papillary projections, thick septations and increased vascularity, with ascites
explanation: The IOTA simple rules and the risk of malignancy index, which combines ultrasound score, menopausal status and CA-125, formalise this assessment.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (placenta accreta investigations), 2022 INI-CET (hydatidiform mole on USG)

subject: Radiology
stem: The imaging modality of choice for staging rectal carcinoma locally is
options: MRI of the pelvis, to assess the mesorectal fascia and circumferential resection margin
explanation: MRI predicts whether total mesorectal excision will achieve a clear margin and so determines who needs neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. Endorectal ultrasound is better for very early T1 and T2 lesions.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (ulcerative colitis on CT), 2017 AIIMS (mushroom cap sign in rectal endometriosis)

subject: Radiology
stem: The Fleischner guidelines are used for
options: Follow-up of incidentally detected pulmonary nodules
explanation: Interval and modality depend on nodule size, solid or subsolid character, number and the patient's risk. Nodules under 6 mm in a low-risk patient need no routine follow-up.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (CORADS 5 typical for COVID), 2023 INI-CET (CECT for lung carcinoma)

subject: Radiology
stem: Gadolinium-based contrast is contraindicated when the eGFR is below 30 because of the risk of
explanation: Linear chelates carry the highest risk; macrocyclic agents are far safer. Iodinated contrast causes **contrast-induced nephropathy** instead, and metformin is the drug withheld because of lactic acidosis.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (non-ionic contrast has lower osmolality), 2021 NEET-PG (contrast reaction management)

subject: Radiology
stem: The absolute contraindication to MRI is
options: A cardiac pacemaker or implanted defibrillator that is not MR-conditional, and an intraocular ferromagnetic foreign body
explanation: Cochlear implants and ferromagnetic aneurysm clips are the other classics. Titanium and modern stents are safe, and a copper IUCD is not a contraindication.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (MRI does not use ionising radiation), 2023 INI-CET (modality of choice in soft tissue)

subject: Radiology
stem: BI-RADS 4 on mammography means
options: A suspicious abnormality, for which biopsy should be considered
A benign finding needing no action
explanation: Category 0 is incomplete, 1 negative, 2 benign, 3 probably benign with short-interval follow-up, 4 suspicious, 5 highly suggestive and 6 biopsy-proven malignancy.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (microcalcification in breast on mammography), 2017 AIIMS (comet tail sign)

subject: Radiology
stem: The mammographic finding most suspicious for malignancy is
options: Fine pleomorphic or linear-branching microcalcification with a spiculated mass
explanation: Popcorn calcification indicates an involuting fibroadenoma and rim calcification a cyst or fat necrosis. Architectural distortion and skin or nipple retraction are the other malignant signs.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (microcalcification in breast on mammography), 2020 INI-CET (modality of choice in dense breast)

subject: Radiology
stem: Ultrasound is preferred over mammography for a breast lump in
options: A woman under 30 years, in whom dense breast tissue reduces mammographic sensitivity
explanation: Screening mammography begins at 40 to 50 depending on the guideline. MRI is added for BRCA carriers and for assessing extent before breast conservation.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (modality of choice in dense breast — ultrasound), 2021 INI-CET (breast imaging)

subject: Radiology
stem: The Bosniak classification is used for
options: Renal cystic lesions, to predict the risk of malignancy
explanation: Category I and II are benign, IIF needs follow-up, III is indeterminate with roughly a 50% malignancy rate and IV is treated as malignant. Enhancement and thick septations drive the category up.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (renal cell carcinoma staging), 2018 AIIMS (bear paw sign in xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis)

subject: Radiology
stem: LI-RADS 5 on triple-phase CT of a cirrhotic liver requires
options: Arterial phase hyperenhancement with washout in the portal venous or delayed phase, in a nodule above 10 mm
explanation: This pattern is diagnostic of hepatocellular carcinoma in a cirrhotic liver **without biopsy**. Haemangioma shows progressive centripetal filling and persistent enhancement instead.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (hepatocellular carcinoma imaging), 2015 AIIMS (calcifications in liver)

subject: Radiology
stem: The CT severity index in acute pancreatitis grades
options: The extent of pancreatic necrosis together with peripancreatic inflammation and collections
Only the size of the pancreas
explanation: Contrast CT is best performed **72 hours after onset**, since necrosis is not yet apparent earlier. The revised Atlanta classification separates interstitial oedematous from necrotising pancreatitis.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (acute pancreatitis investigations), 2024 INI-CET (chain of lakes in chronic pancreatitis, 2X)

subject: Radiology
stem: RECIST criteria assess
options: Tumour response to treatment, by the change in the sum of the longest diameters of target lesions
Radiation dose to organs at risk
explanation: A 30% decrease is a partial response and a 20% increase or any new lesion is progression. Lymph nodes are measured in the **short** axis, and PERCIST uses metabolic rather than size change.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (PET-CT uses FDG), 2014 AIIMS (tumour response assessment)

subject: Radiology
stem: The imaging window within which thrombolysis may be offered in acute ischaemic stroke, and the score used to quantify early CT change, are
options: 1 hour, and the Hunt and Hess grade
explanation: ASPECTS scores 10 middle cerebral artery regions, subtracting a point for each with early ischaemic change; below 6 predicts poor outcome. Mechanical thrombectomy extends to 6 to 24 hours with perfusion selection.
exam: 2021 NEET-PG (lacunar infarct on CT), 2020 INI-CET (Spetzler-Martin score for AVM)

subject: Radiology
stem: CT perfusion in acute stroke identifies salvageable tissue as
options: A region with prolonged mean transit time but preserved cerebral blood volume
A region with reduced cerebral blood volume
explanation: That mismatch is the ischaemic **penumbra**. Reduced cerebral blood volume marks the infarct core, which will not recover and predicts haemorrhagic transformation if reperfused.
exam: 2021 NEET-PG (lacunar infarct), 2022 INI-CET (DWI in acute infarct)

subject: Radiology
stem: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunting is indicated for
options: Refractory variceal bleeding and refractory ascites in portal hypertension
explanation: The shunt runs from the hepatic vein to the portal vein. **Hepatic encephalopathy** is the main complication, because the diverted blood bypasses hepatic detoxification.
exam: 2019 NEET-PG (percutaneous biliary drainage, 2X), 2022 INI-CET (portal hypertension imaging)

subject: Radiology
stem: An inferior vena caval filter is placed when
options: Anticoagulation has failed or is contraindicated in a patient with venous thromboembolism
A patient has an arterial embolus
explanation: It is sited infrarenally and retrievable filters should be removed once anticoagulation is safe, since long-term dwelling raises the risk of caval thrombosis and filter fracture.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG (pulmonary embolism on CT, 2X), 2017 AIIMS (filling defect in pulmonary artery)

subject: Radiology
stem: Uterine artery embolisation is most often performed for
explanation: Polyvinyl alcohol or gelatin particles are used. Post-embolisation syndrome with pain and fever is expected, and the procedure is avoided when future fertility is a priority.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (placenta accreta spectrum imaging), 2022 INI-CET (hydatidiform mole on USG)

subject: Radiology
stem: The resistive index on Doppler ultrasound is calculated as
options: (Peak systolic velocity − end diastolic velocity) ÷ peak systolic velocity
Peak systolic velocity ÷ end diastolic velocity
explanation: A raised index indicates downstream vascular resistance, as in renal parenchymal disease or transplant rejection. In the umbilical artery, **absent or reversed end-diastolic flow** indicates severe fetal compromise.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (Doppler in IUGR), 2023 INI-CET (umbilical artery Doppler)

subject: Radiology
stem: Elastography is used clinically to
options: Grade hepatic fibrosis non-invasively and characterise thyroid and breast nodules by stiffness
explanation: Transient elastography reduces the need for liver biopsy in chronic hepatitis and fatty liver disease. Malignant tissue is stiffer than benign tissue, which underlies nodule assessment.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (hepatic imaging), 2022 INI-CET (ultrasound in chronic liver disease)

subject: Radiology
stem: The TI-RADS system classifies
options: Thyroid nodules on ultrasound, to decide which need fine-needle aspiration
explanation: Marked hypoechogenicity, a taller-than-wide shape, irregular margins, microcalcification and extrathyroidal extension are the suspicious features. The size threshold for aspiration falls as the category rises.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (thyroid scintigraphy), 2017 AIIMS (cold nodule on thyroid scan)

subject: Radiology
stem: The commonest indication for image-guided percutaneous drainage rather than surgery is
options: A well-defined unilocular abscess with a safe access route and no necrotic debris
A multiloculated collection with thick debris
explanation: Ultrasound or CT guidance with the Seldinger technique achieves high success rates for liver, appendicular and tubo-ovarian abscesses, avoiding laparotomy.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (amoebic liver abscess management), 2015 AIIMS (liver abscess imaging)

subject: Radiology
stem: The average effective dose of a CT of the abdomen and pelvis, compared with a chest radiograph, is approximately
options: 10 mSv against 0.02 mSv — about 400 to 500 times greater
explanation: A mammogram is about 0.4 mSv and a PET-CT 15 to 25 mSv. Natural background radiation is roughly 2 to 3 mSv a year, which is the figure these doses are usually set against.
exam: 2023 NEET-PG (inverse square law, 2X), 2016 AIIMS (radiation exposure limits)

subject: Radiology
stem: Dose reduction in paediatric CT is achieved mainly by
options: Weight-based tube current modulation, lowering kVp, limiting the scan range and avoiding repeat phases
explanation: Children are more radiosensitive and have longer to express a stochastic effect, which is the basis of the Image Gently campaign. Ultrasound and MRI are substituted wherever they answer the question.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (radiation exposure limit), 2022 INI-CET (modality avoiding ionising radiation)
